findings.title: Crash-left staging files cannot be recovered; post-link leftovers also block immutable-version reads
findings.spec: PRODUCT_DESIGN.md 3.0.2 section 20.4: immutable secret write before CAS; orphan versions must be recoverably cleanable.
findings.trigger: Abrupt process exit after a .staging-<uuid> file has been created/written and before the finally unlink; includes the window immediately after os.link publishes the immutable filename.
findings.current_behavior: FileSecretStore.versions() enumerates only secret_<32hex>. cleanup_orphan_secrets() uses only that enumeration. A staging-only file is never selected. If link already succeeded, the staging and immutable names share an inode with st_nlink=2; _read rejects it, so read/available and deletion through delete->_read fail closed instead of recovering that locally-created state.
findings.impact: No claimed unauthorized generation or public secret leak. The promised orphan recovery is incomplete, and a crash can leave a valid newly written private version (or fingerprint-key publication) unavailable until manual filesystem intervention.
findings.minimum_followup: Owner should serialize initialize/put/recovery at the storage level; safely recognize only its own staging artifacts, validate type/owner/mode and avoid symlinks, recover before removing unreferenced immutable versions. Do not delete a concurrently active writer staging file merely by name.
needed_verification: Real subprocess exit at the pre-link window, followed by cleanup with private bytes removed.
Real subprocess exit after link but before unlink: recover nlink=2 staging state, preserve any committed referenced version, then clean true orphans.
Concurrent initialize/put versus cleanup cannot remove an active temporary version.
findings.evidence_limit: Read-only static review; no tests, process-kill probe, browser, network, credential access or code edit performed by this reviewer. B independently confirmed no other staging recovery implementation exists and accepted the candidate for verification.

checked_without_new_blocking_finding: Complete command HMAC binds stable single-user workspace actor, route, key, payload and version preconditions. Secret commands persist a redacted command body and private HMAC, not secret bytes or ordinary public secret hashes.

Original config/secret/grant/revoke ACK replays validate the relevant immutable history prefix before new-operation CAS; academic Policy precedes consent summary/replay access. Later current reads and old ACK values remain distinct.

Configuration reference existence is historical secret_present; physical unreadability does not rewrite it. Secret writes append immutable versions and commit CAS+safe ACK together; commit uncertainty does not immediately delete a possibly referenced version.

Frozen proposal reads validate canonical bytes, complete material/snapshot/message/reference digests, provider revision and original ACK bindings. Grant history, source binding and receipt join the caller transaction.

One consent reserves at most one dispatch, usage is monotonic and nullable, and terminal/UTF8 channel artifacts are validated together and written under SAVEPOINT. Identical terminal replay preserves the original; different terminal/bytes are rejected.

Backup sanitization requires an independent copy, validates native history first, removes private fingerprint/locator rows, preserves immutable historical audit bytes and records a checked dispatch-disabled projection. Export packing/checkpoint/VACUUM are caller responsibilities, not proof supplied by this static review.

Unknown source registry and confirmed preparation changes are distinguished from integrity corruption in proposal diagnostics. Dispatch views still require a real source-owned JobRef and may safely reject readback if that owner is unavailable; no fabricated JobRef/status fallback was found.
Migration creates deferred command references, unique proposal/consent/dispatch relationships and immutable-history triggers; legacy provider rows are not automatically accepted as native grants.
